Source slide page 3 (extracted text):
ENGINEERING CHEMISTRY 
Functional materials - Polymers

Molecular weight of Polymers
Polymers are a mix of chains of different lengths
Weight of polymers is expressed as an average molecular weight
The molecular weight is an important characteristic of a polymer sample as several properties of polymers depend on the molecular weight
The entire range of mechanical properties like stress-strain, impact, fracture, fatigue, creep, stress relaxation and cracking are influenced by average molecular weight and molecular weight distribution

Source slide page 4 (extracted text):

Number average molecular weight

Average molecular weight

Source slide page 5 (extracted text):
ENGINEERING CHEMISTRY 
Functional materials - Polymers

Number average molecular weight, 
 Obtained by dividing the total weight of the dispersed material with the total number of polymer units present

where n1, n2, n3 …. are number of polymer units having molecular weights M1, M2, M3,…. respectively

where ni is the number of polymer units of molecular mass Mi
It depends only on number of polymer units and not their size
Colligative properties like osmotic pressure, elevation in  boiling point or depression in melting point is used to determine number average molecular weight

Source slide page 6 (extracted text):
ENGINEERING CHEMISTRY 
Functional materials - Polymers

Weight average molecular weight, 

   It gives representation to various molecular species in
    proportion to their masses in the given material
   In the averaging process, the molecular weight of each
    individual species is multiplied by its mass

where m1, m2, m3 …. are masses of polymer units having molecular weights M1, M2, M3 respectively

if n1, n2, n3 …. are number of polymer units having

  then m1 = n1M1, m2 = n2 M2 ….

Source slide page 8 (extracted text):
ENGINEERING CHEMISTRY 
Functional materials - Polymers

The ratio            is called the polydispersity index (PDI) 
 
It is a measure for the broadness of a molecular weight distribution of a polymer, that is, the larger the polydispersity index, the broader the molecular weight distribution
A monodisperse polymer where all the chain lengths are equal has  PDI =1
PDI > 1, shows that the polymeric sample is less homogeneous and polydisperse
